topic: K1 define a trace-aware colored fixing calculus for finite positive regular-maximal labeled-missingness graphs, allowing fixing before context restriction. K2 prove every returned observed-law functional sound. K3 prove completeness by returning a colored hedge and two positive same-observed/different-query lm-SCMs. K4 give a terminating finite procedure without claiming polynomial time. Include the Figure 3(b) fix-then-select witness and ADHD medication/test-achievement FATE/NATE consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a finite trace-aware colored fixing calculus for NATE recovery in positive regular-maximal lm-graphs that permits causal fixing before missingness-context restriction and is sound and complete for every observed-proxy-law query.

source_refs.claim: Figure 3(b) is recoverable only by applying do-calculus before selecting R_W=0, and the authors state that broad NATE recovery criteria remain open.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Leonard Henckel, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.claim: The CSI-calculus and automated search are sound but not complete, and nonidentifiability with context-specific independencies is NP-hard.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Missing-data recovery uses recursive variable-set removal under a partial order and handles induced selection and hidden-variable subproblems, but has no lm-label trace semantics.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser, James M. Robins

source_refs.excerpt: district-compositional signed order-AMWN/ctf-calculus with a terminal local-trace compiler is not delivered
Districtwise atom probabilities cannot simply be selected independently

open_problems.why_unsolved: De Aguas et al. provide only sufficient criteria and exhibit the exact order-sensitive obstruction: Figure 3(b) first derives P(Y|do(A),R_W) and only then selects R_W=0. Tikka et al. can manipulate CSI information but do not give a complete calculus or missing-proxy trace semantics, while Bhattacharya et al. recursively recover missing-data kernels without labels whose licenses switch by context. The prior CausalSmith calculus project adds a second concrete warning: global response-function equality does not automatically decompose into independently selectable district atoms. The missing proof step is a colored reachable-kernel invariant that carries both its observed-data trace and licensing labels through fixing, marginalization, district decomposition, and later restriction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating recursion on colored reachable districts that returns an observed-proxy-law functional equal to P(Y|do(A)) on every success branch, derives the Figure 3(b) functional P(Y|A,R_W=0), and is equivalent to query constancy over the finite positive lm-SCM fiber.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from missingness-induced downstream mechanism shifts to FATE/NATE and then to the precise failure of context-first recovery.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ordinary m-graphs forbid substantive descendants of missingness indicators -> lm-graphs encode missingness-driven mechanism shifts -> Figure 3(b) shows context-first recovery loses an identifiable NATE -> a fix-before-restrict complete calculus is needed

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the CSI-calculus's sound context-labeled intervention rules, replacing unrestricted term search by recursion over colored reachable kernels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest sound calculus for labeled context-specific causal models, but it lacks missing-data trace semantics and completeness.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt recursive set removal under a partial order, including subproblems that induce selection or latent structure, while attaching label licenses and trace provenance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its recursion addresses the same observed-proxy-to-target-law obstruction; the new step is delayed restriction with colored legality.

method_exemplars.technique: Read nuisance regressions and missingness weights from each returned trace factor, extend the graph-specific doubly robust score, and prove asymptotic linearity by recursive conditioning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already supplies doubly robust inference for the exact FATE/NATE targets on a special lm-graph, giving a concrete estimation rung for a general returned functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Find a colored-hedge criterion that is necessary and sufficient for NATE nonrecoverability in finite positive regular-maximal lm-graphs and is realizable by two strictly positive lm-SCMs with identical observed proxy laws but different query values.

source_refs.claim: The authors warn that combining CSI-calculus with missing-data recovery is not guaranteed complete, leaving a converse certificate for failed recovery unresolved.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Leonard Henckel, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.claim: Ordinary ID failure returns a hedge and supports paired observationally equivalent models, but the construction does not preserve lm-label trace laws or strict positivity.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: Positivity conditions interact with Q-decomposition and identification algorithms and must be propagated explicitly rather than added after identification.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, Sanghack Lee

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the unrestricted global response-law simplex with a latent-DAG or district-factorized response-type construction
Prove an alphabet-lifting or binary-witness sufficiency result

open_problems.why_unsolved: An ordinary hedge equates one observational distribution, whereas an lm certificate must equate every coarsened proxy trace while respecting mandatory label deletions, missingness-triggered mechanism shifts, latent-district factorization, and regular-maximality. The failed CS-hedge proposal found that an unrestricted response-law null direction may not factor through a legal latent graph and that binary parity witnesses may be invalidated by mandatory label deletion. In addition, usual deterministic hedge pairs can contain zero cells; an epsilon perturbation can destroy exact observed-trace equality or label-specific independencies. No located result proves a trace-valid, strictly positive realization for every failed lm recursion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if colored-hedge theorem with an explicit finite response-function compiler that maps every genuine failure trace to two strictly positive regular-maximal lm-SCMs sharing the complete observed proxy-and-indicator law but disagreeing on P(Y|do(A)), or a minimal counterexample delimiting positivity or alphabet sufficiency.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the exact completeness gap for NATE recovery and explains why merely combining existing sound procedures may still miss recoverable cases.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: lm-graphs reveal recovery information absent from the underlying m-graph -> current criteria are only sufficient -> completeness must explain every failed recursion -> a positive colored hedge supplies the missing nonrecoverability certificate

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt ID's failure-to-hedge extraction and paired-SCM construction, replacing ordinary C-forests by label-compatible trace-colored forests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical bridge from recursive identification failure to a finite graphical obstruction and two same-observed, different-interventional models.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode response functions, observed proxy cells, label constraints, positivity floors, and the query as polynomial constraints, then extract separated feasible solutions to guide the analytic witness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its polynomial program can enforce exact same-observed restrictions with nonresponse and selection while testing whether the query varies.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when legal colored fixing commutes with missingness-context restriction, and when restricting first irreversibly loses an identifying trace kernel available to fix-then-restrict.

source_refs.claim: Ordinary nested Markov theory makes reachable kernels independent of a valid fixing sequence, but only within one CADMG and one kernel domain.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Figure 3(b) proves operation order can matter: do-calculus before selecting R_W=0 recovers a query that a context-by-context sequence misses.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Leonard Henckel, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.excerpt: ordinary conditional or nested/fixing c-factor request is first typed
Add an explicit mapping from each typed source-cover input to the corresponding systematic-selection data-fusion input

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary sequence invariance compares kernel divisions inside a fixed CADMG. A colored lm step may be licensed only on one context slice, while restriction can delete a labeled edge, remove a variable needed to derive a denominator, or change the proxy-law cells on which positivity holds. The prior source-cover proposal addresses an analogous issue by typing each nested request with the graph where it was extracted, but it never proves an lm-specific commutation theorem. Thus the ordinary adjacent-swap argument must be strengthened to transport operation licenses, trace provenance, and positivity domains; Figure 3(b) shows that unrestricted commutation is false at the level of available information.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient colored adjacent-swap theorem giving graphical and support conditions under which fixing sequences and context restriction produce the same trace kernel, together with a minimal regular-maximal lm-graph and explicit functional for every noncommuting obstruction class.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Figure 3(b) makes operation order a substantive source of identifying information rather than a computational detail.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: labels are valid only in missingness contexts -> recovery may need operations before entering a context -> restriction can erase the derivation trace -> characterize exactly when fix and restrict commute

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt fixing-sequence invariance by reducing legal orders to adjacent swaps and proving equality of the corresponding kernel divisions while carrying colors and trace domains.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is exactly a context-indexed analogue of the sequence invariance that makes ordinary nested fixing well-defined.

method_exemplars.technique: Port nested-kernel nuisance estimation and influence-function expansion to the noncommuting fix-then-select functional under trace-specific positive cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The successful noncommuting branch returns a nested functional whose empirical implementation must preserve the same extraction order.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify the smallest finite lm-graphs for which fix-then-restrict identifies NATE but every restrict-then-identify strategy fails, and determine whether Figure 3(b) is the unique minimal obstruction up to labeled-graph equivalence.

source_refs.claim: Figure 3(b) gives one explicit fix-before-restrict witness but no minimality or exhaustive small-graph characterization.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Leonard Henckel, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.claim: Finite discrete causal problems with selection, measurement error, and nonresponse can be encoded as exact response-function polynomial programs that test point identification.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Context-specific identification is NP-hard, so a bounded exact classification is a meaningful validation target even without a polynomial-time general algorithm.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Figure 3(b) establishes existence but not the combinatorial reason delayed restriction is necessary. The response-function polynomial method supplies a finite semantic oracle, but its published model has no lm-specific shifted-mechanism labels or explicit comparison of operation orders. Searches for colored or trace-aware fixing combined with labeled missingness graphs found no occupied classification. The first changed step is to encode every missingness-triggered shifted mechanism and observed proxy trace as shared equality constraints before comparing the fix-first and restrict-first recovery closures.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An isomorphism-reduced enumeration through an explicit vertex and alphabet bound, certified by exact response-function elimination, plus either a necessary-and-sufficient graphical pattern for all minimal fix-before-restrict witnesses or a second nonisomorphic minimal witness disproving uniqueness of Figure 3(b).

writing_exemplar.why: Figure 3(b) is the destination phenomenon and provides the cleanest motivation for an exhaustive minimal-obstruction study.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: context-first decomposition is complete in restricted labeled models -> Figure 3(b) defeats it despite recoverability -> its minimal and canonical status is unknown -> classify every smallest fix-before-restrict witness

method_exemplars.technique: Translate each finite lm-SCM into compatible response-type probabilities and polynomial constraints, then certify point identification or return two feasible models with separated query values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the exact computational oracle needed to audit the calculus on small finite graphs with nonresponse and selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Use elimination ideals and symbolic identifiability checks to turn response-function calculations into exact algebraic equality certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution requires a mathematical classification of determining traces, not only numerical endpoint comparisons.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an estimator compiler for smooth FATE and NATE functionals returned by a trace-aware lm-graph recovery calculus, with influence-function representations and cross-fitted asymptotic normality under explicit trace-specific positivity conditions.

source_refs.claim: The lm-graph paper derives doubly robust FATE and NATE estimators for one application-motivated graph, not arbitrary recovered trace functionals.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Leonard Henckel, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.claim: Doubly robust estimators combine outcome and missingness or treatment models and retain consistency when one member of a nuisance pair is correct.
source_refs.author: Heejung Bang, James M. Robins

source_refs.claim: Identification formulas carry formula-specific positivity requirements that can be elicited with Q-decomposition, but the work does not compile estimators.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, Sanghack Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: A general colored calculus may return sums and products of kernels learned on different missingness traces, so neither a complete-case influence function nor one missingness-pattern score applies mechanically. De Aguas et al. derive doubly robust scores only for a single ADHD-motivated graph, and positivity-aware formula production does not provide pathwise derivatives or limit theory. The first proof step that changes is the derivative recursion: every trace-specific conditional law contributes its own observation-probability weight and nested-regression term, with compatibility conditions when one colored kernel is reused across branches.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A recursive map from every smooth returned colored functional to an observed-data influence function and cross-fitted estimator, with a theorem giving consistency, asymptotic linearity, a Gaussian limit, and valid Wald coverage under stated nuisance-rate and trace-positivity assumptions.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects FATE/NATE to the ADHD medication and test-achievement application and shows why the two targets require different regressions across missingness contexts.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: missingness changes downstream mechanisms -> FATE and NATE answer different policy questions -> special-case doubly robust estimators show feasible inference -> arbitrary identified trace functionals need automatic valid inference

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize iterated-regression and inverse-probability augmentation, proving mean-zero scores and robustness by telescoping conditional expectations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Colored trace functionals jointly involve causal and missing-data nuisance mechanisms, the setting for which augmented doubly robust arguments were designed.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift the graph-specific FATE/NATE scores to a recursion indexed by colored fixing steps and observed traces, retaining their nuisance-orthogonality argument at each base case.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the only located work deriving estimators for these exact lm-SCM targets and supplies base cases the compiler must reproduce.

literature_map:
de Aguas, Henckel, Pensar, and Biele (UAI 2025; arXiv:2506.15441) introduce lm-SCMs, lm-graphs, FATE, and NATE, but give only sufficient recovery criteria.
Their Figure 3(b) is decisive: P(Y|do(A),R_W) is derived before selecting R_W=0, yielding P(Y|A,R_W=0); context-first decomposition misses it.
They explicitly say general NATE recovery is challenging and that combining CSI-calculus with missing-DAG recovery is not guaranteed complete.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (NeurIPS 2019; arXiv:2009.09768) give a sound CSI-calculus and search, prove NP-hardness, and do not obtain general completeness.
Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash (AISTATS 2022; arXiv:2110.12064) prove completeness only when CSI context variables are observed causal roots.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (UAI 2020; arXiv:1907.00241) recursively recover laws under missing-data DAGs but do not represent lm-label traces.
Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (ICML 2020; arXiv:2004.04872) give complete full-law criteria, while query recovery can succeed beyond full-law recovery.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (Annals of Statistics 2023; arXiv:1701.06686) supply ordinary fixing, reachability, intrinsic kernels, and sequence invariance.
Shpitser and Pearl's ID completeness work supplies hedges and paired countermodels, but not strictly positive trace-colored lm-SCM witnesses.
Mohan and Pearl (JASA 2021; arXiv:1801.03583) systematize m-graph recovery and testability while excluding substantive descendants of missingness indicators.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (JASA 2023; arXiv:2109.13471) provide exact finite response-function polynomial programs for selection, measurement error, and nonresponse.
Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee (ICML 2024) show positivity must be tracked with Q-decomposition rather than appended after identification.
Bang and Robins (Biometrics 2005), together with de Aguas et al.'s special lm estimators, provide an inference substrate but no general trace-functional compiler.
Searches for colored fixing, trace-aware fixing, or nested fixing combined with lm-graphs found no paper occupying the confluence, colored-hedge, or small-graph classification targets.
